name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 190 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 23% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 190 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 23 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Security forces in Kashmir have killed the last known local Lashkar operative, and Amit Shah has repeatedly declared that no local terrorists remain in the valley. In Manipur, security troops are conducting operations after a spurious liquor tragedy that left over 300 hospitalised and 13 dead, while DGP Nalin Prabhat reviews ongoing security actions in the Jammu zone. In Chhattisgarh, forces recovered arms, ammunition and explosives from Maoist dumps in Dantewada and Kondagaon. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Sikkerhetsstyrker i Kashmir har drept den siste kjente lokale Lashkar-operatøren, og Amit Shah har gjentatte ganger erklært at ingen lokale terrorister lenger finnes i dalen. I Manipur utfører sikkerhetstroppene operasjoner etter en falsk alkoholtragedie som førte til over 300 innlagte og 13 døde, mens DGP Nalin Prabhat gjennomgår pågående sikkerhetstiltak i Jammu-sonen. I Chhattisgarh har styrker funnet våpen, ammunisjon og sprengstoff i maoistiske lager i Dantewada og Kondagaon. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
